sights.w: 1830s home of abolitionists Ridgeway and Sarah Haines, a station on the Underground Railroad — freedom-seekers hid in the attic. National Register (1974); restored by the Alliance Area Preservation Society and one of 15 stops on Ohio's Underground Railroad Trail. Tours first weekend monthly, Feb–Nov.

George F. Hammond's 1895 Beaux-Arts courthouse wrapped around the 1870s building, its clock tower crowned by four trumpeting angels, the 'Trumpeters of Justice'. Where young William McKinley began his law career. Free to view.
5,000+ acres around the 2,650-acre Michael J. Kirwan Reservoir (Army Corps, 1965; state park since 1966): beach, boating, camping and about 12 miles of single-track mountain-bike loops.
234-acre Portage Park District woods on glacial kettle Lake Pippin, with the 2,000-year-old Hopewell Towner (Lake Pippin) Mound and the 1913 Brady interlocking switch tower; open since 1975. Free.

sights.address: Kenmore Blvd (12th–17th St SW; pin at Lay's Guitar Shop, 974 Kenmore Blvd), Akron, OH 44314
sights.w: Main street of the former city of Kenmore (annexed 1929), the first Akron neighbourhood business district on the National Register (2019): intact streetcar-era storefronts, live-music venues, recording studios and Lay's Guitar Shop (50+ years).
